nary_nodes.label: Analysis of toddler foods
evidence: Four out of five foods sold for toddlers in the United States are ultraprocessed, according to research that analyzed more than 2,700 products on grocery store shelves.

nary_nodes.label: Presentation of findings
evidence: “We found toddler products which failed to meet WHO standards on sugar were four times as likely to be ultraprocessed,” said Hudson, who presented the preliminary research findings on Sunday at the annual meeting of the American Society for Nutrition.

nary_nodes.label: FDA proposed front‑of‑package labeling rule
evidence: The US Food and Drug Administration proposed a rule in 2025 for a mandatory, front-of-package labeling system for most packaged foods that would rate a food as “low,” “medium” or “high” in added sugars, sodium and saturated fat.

nary_nodes.label: January study on baby‑food additives
evidence: Prior research published in January found over 70% of 651 baby and toddler foods contained additives that emerging research has linked to inflammation and disruptions in the gut microbiome.

nary_nodes.label: 80% of toddler foods are ultraprocessed
evidence: Four out of five foods sold for toddlers in the United States are ultraprocessed, according to research that analyzed more than 2,700 products on grocery store shelves.
“The answer is over 80% of the products are ultraprocessed,” Hudson said.

nary_nodes.label: Nearly half of toddler foods failed WHO nutrition benchmark
evidence: Nearly half of those items also failed to meet at least one nutritional benchmark for children set by the World Health Organization.

nary_nodes.label: Many toddler foods high in sugar and sodium
evidence: “Many of them are high in sugar, high in sodium, but parents really cannot tell that from just walking down the aisle.”

nary_nodes.label: Products failing WHO sugar standards four times as likely ultraprocessed
evidence: “We found toddler products which failed to meet WHO standards on sugar were four times as likely to be ultraprocessed,” said Hudson, who presented the preliminary research findings on Sunday at the annual meeting of the American Society for Nutrition.

nary_nodes.label: Almost a quarter of foods higher in sodium than recommended
evidence: “Almost a quarter of the foods were higher in sodium than is recommended, and some were high in fat and calorie dense,” she added.

nary_nodes.label: Ultraprocessed foods crowd out healthier options
evidence: “The problem isn’t just what’s in these high-sugar, high-salt ultraprocessed foods, it’s what they crowd out,” said Jane Houlihan, research director for Healthy Babies Bright Futures, an alliance of nonprofits, scientists and donors with a mission of reducing babies’ exposures to neurotoxic chemicals.

nary_nodes.label: Toddler eating snack foods likely eats fewer whole grains etc.
evidence: “A toddler who fills up on fruit snacks, sweetened yogurt, crackers and snack bars is likely to eat fewer whole grains, vegetables, beans and other healthier foods,” Houlihan said in an email.

nary_nodes.label: Parents cannot tell ultraprocessed nature by aisle
evidence: “Many of them are high in sugar, high in sodium, but parents really cannot tell that from just walking down the aisle.”

nary_nodes.label: Industry markets toddler foods as healthy but not true
evidence: “Industry has marketed this toddler foods to make parents believe these foods were created for the health of toddlers, and it’s just not true.”

nary_nodes.label: No universal definition of ultraprocessed food
evidence: There is currently no universally accepted scientific definition of the term ‘ultraprocessed’ food, a spokesperson said.

nary_nodes.label: 71% of baby foods’ top ingredient is additives
evidence: “What shocked me was the top ingredient in 71% of these baby foods wasn’t a fruit or vegetable — it was one or more additives,” Elizabeth Dunford, an adjunct assistant professor of nutrition at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, told CNN previously.

type_definitions.definition: A sovereign nation-state with defined territory and government.
A classification of foods based on target consumer, purpose, or processing level.
A tier within a processing classification system that groups foods by degree of industrial processing.
An individual human being.
An organized establishment, often academic or medical, that provides services or conducts research.
A collective entity such as a professional society, nonprofit, or industry group.
A governmental body with regulatory or administrative authority.
A formal rule, guideline, or standard issued by an authority.
A systematic framework used to categorize items, such as foods, based on defined criteria.
A dietary component such as sugar, sodium, fat, or calories that contributes to nutrition.
A group of food ingredients sharing a functional or chemical property, such as additives.
A numeric quantity representing the amount of items.
A geographic place, such as a city or region.
A specific marketed food item intended for consumption.
A systematic examination of data to derive findings.
An event where research findings are formally shared with an audience.
A suggested rule or regulation put forward by a governmental agency.
An earlier published study that provides background evidence.
A statement asserting the proportion or frequency of a condition.
A claim that a product does not meet a specified standard.
A statement about the level of a specific nutrient in a product.
A claim linking a product characteristic to its likelihood of belonging to a processing category.
A claim specifically about sodium levels in foods.
A claim that one type of food reduces consumption of healthier alternatives.
A claim that a certain diet pattern leads to reduced intake of other food groups.
A claim about what consumers can or cannot perceive regarding a product.
A claim that marketing messages inaccurately portray a product’s healthfulness.
A claim that a universally accepted definition does not exist.
A claim about the proportion of products containing additives.

Denotes the subject matter or focus of a claim, event, or statement.
Indicates that a food category contains a high level of a particular nutrient.
Shows that a product or category does not satisfy a specified benchmark or standard.
Describes a situation where one type of food reduces the consumption of healthier alternatives.
Indicates that a presentation or talk was delivered at a specific meeting or conference.
Specifies the agency or body that put forward a regulatory proposal.
Shows that an organization created or issued a policy or guideline.
Indicates the scope or target of a policy, rule, or guideline.
Denotes that a classification system assigns items to a particular category.
States that a category contains a particular item or sub‑category.
Specifies the numeric quantity associated with an event or entity.
Indicates the geographic location where an event occurred.
